reviews.text: 停！看到这里的记得明天再玩。免得一口气玩完了
我其实挺喜欢这种类型的游戏的，比如说lyca，但是对于一名年岁上来后不再反应灵敏的成就党来说，这个全程一次不死的成就真的是天崩类型了。（不会真的有人对成就看得那么重吧？有的，兄弟，有的）当然对于demo就玩得比较尽兴来说还是会给好评的。

中文技能名很有趣很有梗的弹幕射击游戏，想那几个贵贵的技能树拓展节点的全名的时候应该没少费脑细胞吧hhhh 玩Demo的时候以为会是个爽游，结果正式版意外还挺难的，光是躲敌机弹幕其实倒是也还好，但居然还要被场景追着杀，体验就还蛮奇妙的…而且，在把Boss打到残血的时候也是经常要么时间到了，要么马失前蹄，总之和我想象中的靠不断重置或是肝来实现秒天秒地的“解压”“增量”游戏可能不太一样。 不过游戏还是蛮有趣的，最终Boss的弹幕演出也很棒，唯一的缺点是要一直按住鼠标（加速）躲弹幕，有点费中老年人的手（ 顺便，友情提示，因为同时存在不死成就和死亡次数成就，除非开局就被弹幕之神附体非常顺利的打完3小时30分钟全程不死通关，不然想要全成就肯定需要二周目，因此可以提前做好打算。 我个人反正是在打完一周目之后选择了用部分存档数据覆盖了二周目的存档。虽然可耻，但一模一样的东西再打一遍确实很痛苦，因此也算是通过背板和属性碾压玩了一回爽游。

I liked it until I beat it and tried to get all the achievements. Getting 100% in a game should be fun and challenging, not tedious and annoying. Not getting hit on the last stage isn't about skill, it's all about luck, hoping you don't get hit out of nowhere by an enemy you can't even see cause everything is so cluttered. More luck depending on getting crits so you can actually make any progress. On one attempt I lost simply cause while trying so hard to dodge I ran out of time. I don't want to play through a game I just beat AGAIN, with absolutely no added content either, no challenge, just annoying padding of a game I want to be done with.

Not a very good bullet hell. They create situations where you have no space left to reach your enemies, because you need to be in proximity. The kill speed is also too slow to really handle the amounts of enemies they throw at you. The "complete the game without dying" achievement is basically the devs taking a laugh at you, as the whole game is based on dying and trying again. I don't see how this is achievable.

Even worse is the skills tree runs out before the game does, millions of unusable currency, and beating the final level isn't skill it's 100% luck. I'd wish the developer gave a sh*t about their customers. I don't have the "skill" there is no such thing as "git good" vs unbalanced RNG.

The mid- to late game quickly becomes a miserable slog that turns this game from a reasonably enjoyable incremental into a skills-based (but secretly actually RNG-based) twitch-reaction game. You run out of upgrades long before the final stages, so your only way to beat the stage bosses is to hope real hard that your spawn location RNG is in your favour. If not, you're out of luck. There are numerous times during the final stages where every single inch of real estate on screen is covered by enemy fire, and the phases where this happens are quicker than the recharge on your pulse ability. You can mitigate some of the spam by getting lucky and having the ordinary machines spawn close to you so you can destroy them with your moons, because by this point your turrets and lasers might as well be confetti cannons instead of anything helpful. Again, strictly RNG based. I don't understand the gameplay evolution. The genre and also the first 50-65% of the game are defined by making things easier through incremental progression. The sudden shift into a stat wall while things ramp up sharply in difficulty and pain makes no tonal or logical sense.

[h1][b]咖啡矿工：弹幕增量[/b][/h1] [b]“近期玩过的三款增量游戏中，感觉还行的一部”[/b] 本作让我思考起一个问题，那就是肉鸽游戏和增量游戏的界限在哪里。它似乎就是一款完全依靠肉鸽的局外升级为系统核心的游戏，[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/3862670/_Shelldiver/]龟龟[/url]舆[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/3769130/Keep_on_Mining/]挖矿[/url]的操作性不强，而让我完全忽略了这一点。 4小时左右的流程，各种造成伤害的手段和数值算法颇有新鲜感。相较其他增量游戏，它有一点挑战性，那就是需要靠击杀每个关卡BOSS来获得升级特殊效果用的代币舆前往下一个地图的许可。 相比龟龟更舒服的点在于操作轻松简单，单手即可，无论是鼠标还是键盘，事实上，它有一点点像“幸存者”类游戏，是个十分微妙的定位。此外从头到尾只专注于咖啡豆资源，对咖啡豆的获取增益贯穿始终，而不是一会儿零件一会儿水晶，换一个图就效果清零。 但也正是它加入了弹幕躲避的元素，让部分玩家苦不堪言，看有评论说，全都升满级但还是打不过最终BOSS，以至于死活通不了关，哈哈哈哈。。。好惨！也不好说它有多难，但确实有一点点门槛，增量+弹幕是个新颖的创意，却也让一部分人尝不到乐趣。 P.S.更新了个额外的肉鸽模式，看来制作组也注意到了其重合度舆可能性，但是体验嘛。。。就有点鸡肋

I came at this from more of an incremental gamer than a SHMUP. I had some fun but at a certain point I was unable to progress. The game is far to difficult with really random difficulty spikes that are often pure luck to progress. The tech tree is anemic so that you barely ever seem to get the resources needed to match the level. So if you like me love that incremental games tend to let you manage your own difficulty (and therefore fun) through the tech tree steer clear of this. Maybe people who love bullet hells will adore this but I didn't and with no way to further affect the difficulty this will unfortunately be relegated to my did not finish pile. I'm not going to waste all my gaming time on random luck.

On the border of recommend. It's definitely far more of a bullet hell than heaven, with a bit too much emphasis on picking up mid-run boosts. It also goes in directions I wasn't expecting at the start, but that's in both good and bad aspects. Three things keeping it from a recommend: * final level is too much of a b with so much bullet spam you literally can't avoid certain things (You have a bullet clearer but it's on a long timer) * the upgrades peter out too soon and leave you about at the level you start the game at, just with more tools which is unsatisfying * it's not really an incremental, there's just a lot of grinding to unlock upgrades necessary for progression. 5/10. play something else unless you want a bullet hell with a heavy dash of upgrades mixed in.

game falls apart pretty quickly as the upgrade tree chafes really bad against the shmup style gameplay. the regular levels throw a lot of crap at you without much pattern and forces you into death boxes very often; the asteroids have just enough health that you can't reliably destroy them to navigate around them so frequently you just get bodied on top of being really hard to pick out among all the bullets- this gets stacked with environmental hazards that limits where you can bring your ship even more at complete random. the patterns aren't really helped by how close you have to be to enemies to even damage them, a lot of the time you just have to hope you're on the right side and no random hazard is gonna shove you out of the way - and then the timer compounds on that so your options are to either dodge everything and time out or facetank everything and kind of win this could have just been me picking the wrong options every time but the upgrades never felt like they made much of a difference outside of the pulse and focus ring stuff, most of the time i got something strong it's usually "oh this would have helped earlier but now it does nothing" the multi-stage final boss is actually the easiest part of the game because there's no more random crap and you can actually dodge the patterns it throws out without an asteroid or multiple firefields or random lasers deciding to stall you out or kill you because it's funny

I didn't have a good time with this game, and by the end I just wanted it off my library. It's sold as an incremental bullet hell, but there's no real idle or incremental feel to it. It's grind a stage, fail, grind again, and hope this run is the one where your upgrades are finally high enough. And the grind leans on luck. Whether a run goes well depends a lot on what shows up and how things line up, not on what you did. So you're not really building toward a win, you're rolling the dice and hoping. Beating a boss doesn't feel earned, it feels shallow, like you out-leveled it rather than out-played it. That's the core issue. Your control matters less than your skill tree, but the skill tree isn't satisfying either. It's uninspiring, not empowering. So neither side of the game carries you. Skill doesn't decide the fight, and the upgrades don't feel good to chase. Later stages make it worse. The screen turns into a hot mess. Your bombs, your turrets, asteroids, enemy bullets, and loose chunks all pile up at once until you can barely read what's happening. It's pure chaos, and not the fun kind. You stop dodging on skill and start eating hits you can't even see coming. At that point I wasn't playing, I was just hoping. To be fair, it's short, polished, and runs smooth, and the coffee-vs-SpaceCorp premise has charm. Some people will click with the loop. I didn't, and for me the negatives outweigh everything else.

Astro Prospector is a twin-stick single-screen arcade shooter with "hints of bullet hell" and a big 'ole incremental skill tree. A level in the game unfolds like this: you zip around in your ship mining resources, which draws the attention of the evil monopolistic SpaceCorp goons, who try to shoot you down, only for you to shoot them down instead. You also have a limited amount of time per stage, which is measured in how much drinkable coffee you have in the cockpit. The stage ends either when you're drowsy or when you defeat the 'boss,' and the boss only shows up if you're being enough of a nuisance (both with your haul and in defending yourself). The upgrades are satisfying: multiple mining lasers, longer range, better damage, faster maneuverability, deployable bombs/mines, homing missiles, deployable turrets with their own range and rate of fire, orbiting "moons" that are both defensive and let you ram enemies, a huge pulse wave that 'eats' enemy projectiles, etc. Took me six hours to complete the main campaign and max out the entire skill tree. After that I spent about 20 minutes on the more recent "Endless Coffee" update, which attempts to reorganize the game's mechanics into a rogue-like. This was a fun incremental game, but nothing about the rogue-like version of it was compelling, and there are no shortage of extremely famous/successful rogue-likes for me to get to. For me the best non-idle incremental game on Steam is still Shelldiver, but Astro Prospecter is a fun time. Space Rock Breaker is also pretty good, if you like this one.
